title: Choose LumenLink's composition
question: All three use the same approved visual system; choose the structure that should govern the whole app.

options.label: Twin endpoints
options.lineage: equal Send and Receive entry points
options.thesis: The home screen is one optical link with two equally obvious ends.
options.viewport: A large promise sits beside reciprocal Send and Receive controls joined by the physical light path.
options.risk: The mechanism stays abstract unless the screen and camera labels remain explicit.
options.case: Best for an immediate choice between the two core actions.

options.label: Optical window
options.thesis: A single side-on device scene proves the screen-to-camera mechanism before any explanation.
options.viewport: The promise and actions sit inside one rounded demonstration window with a three-step strip crossing its base.
options.risk: The authored device scene requires the most implementation work and must not imply unsupported browser versions.
options.case: Best mechanism proof and strongest visual memory.

options.label: Product window
options.thesis: The working Send interface is the hero, so trust comes from visible product behavior.
options.viewport: A compact promise and two actions lead into the real file-selection and encryption workflow.
options.risk: Showing Send in detail can make Receive feel secondary.
options.case: Best for frequent users who want to operate immediately.
